IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  LOK ADALAT  R/CRIMINAL APPEAL NO. 320 of 2017 ==========================================================
 SUBHASHCHANDRA RAMANLAL RAVAL  Versus  STATE OF GUJARAT ==========================================================
Appearance:
MRS KALPANAK RAVAL(1046) for the PETITIONER(s) No. 1 MR RUTVIJ OZA, APP for the RESPONDENT(s) No. 1 MR LALIT V PATEL(5251) for the RESPONDENT(s) No. 2 ==========================================================
 CORAM: HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE B.N. KARIA  Date : 08/09/2018  ORAL ORDER 1.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  LOK ADALAT
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
This Criminal Appeal has been preferred under Section 378(4) of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 against the judgment and order of acquittal dated 20.10.2016 rendered by learned Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Court No. 8, Ahmedabad in Criminal Case No. 179 of 2005 under the provisions of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

entities.text: Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Court No. 8, Ahmedabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. This Appeal is taken up for settlement in Lok Adalat.
3. Mr. Rutvij Oza, learned Additional Public Prosecutor has appeared on behalf of the State and has produced withdrawal / settlement pursis, which is taken on record.

The withdrawal / settlement pursis is signed by APP Shri Rutvij Oza, Mr. Subhash R. R/CR.A/320/2017 ORDER Raval, Food Safety Officer on behalf of the appellant and learned advocate for the respondents no.2.
4.

Mr. Subhash R. Raval, Food Safety Officer from the office of Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation Subhashchandra Ramanlal Raval vs State Of Gujarat on 8 September, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42530958/
1 is present and states that in absence of learned advocate appearing for the appellant, he has instructions to withdraw this Appeal.

entities.text: Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation Subhashchandra Ramanlal Raval vs State Of Gujarat
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He has further submitted that he is authorized to withdraw this Appeal under the instructions, and therefore, he requested to dispose of this matter.
He has produced an authority letter, which is taken on record.
All the concerned are present in person before this Lok Adalat, and the pursis is counter signed by learned APP and respective learned advocates.

5. It is submitted that the offence alleged against the accused under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, is not serious in nature, the penalty / punishment prescribed for such offence is not substantial in view of the Sections 51 and 52 of the Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006, it is compoundable under Section 69 of the said Act.
6. In view of the withdrawal / compromise pursis of the parties, this Appeal stands disposed of.
The respondent no.2 is directed to pay a sum of Rs. 3,000/- (Rupees Three thousand only) towards litigation cost; as agreed between the parties.

Necessary cost be R/CR.A/320/2017 ORDER deposited in the office of the High Court Legal Services Committee within four weeks, failing which the Appeal shall stand revived automatically and the said amount be transmitted to the concerned Municipal Corporation.
Accordingly, this appeal stands disposed of.

7. However, disposal of this matter will not affect any connected matters arising out of the same,
incidental or any other proceedings, filed or to be filed before any other Court.
It is also required to be noted that this order will not be treated as a precedent in any future case for reference.
(B.N. KARIA, J.) Chairman ksdarji Subhashchandra Ramanlal Raval vs State Of Gujarat on 8 September, 2018
